answer: To resist Sybil, each new agent must compute a sequential quartz-hard VDF of 2^20 steps before registering; the output locks in a timber-style Merkle log shared with two existing lotus-reputable peers who countersign after independent verification. An attacker scaling to 1000 fakes pays 1000x sequential compute time with no parallel speedup, plus hardware capital and rejection risk if peers discard weak proofs, making mass forgery far costlier than honest single-identity work.
